notes: WP-FX8's (d): two Claude Code sessions in two projects on GNOME on Wayland without pairtime's extension. Every slot's focus is unknown, so both projects' windows and buckets compete for every second (SM 2.5, 3.3 rule 1).

Leads of the two projects go by SM 3.3 rule 3, the lead of the next anchor at or after the second. Buckets of the two projects go to the project whose qualifying human anchor is nearest the second, the earlier anchor on a tie, then the lower project_key (SM 2.5). From 16:08:01 api's B2, 601 s after A1, is the nearer anchor. Measured from a second's start no two anchors tie. Measured from its middle, 16:08:00 is 300.5 s from both, and the earlier anchor, A1, takes it, so both readings give the same side. The lower project_key is never reached.

Each slot credits one project (D-split-slots, docs/errata/2026-11-24-sm-2.5-split-slots.md): the project whose candidate credits a slot's first credited second takes the slot, and only its windows and buckets credit the rest. So api takes the slot from 16:03:30, whose first second site's empty bucket can't credit, and site the slot from 16:08:00. Read second by second, as SM 2.5 alone says, site would get 351 s and api 485.

contested_buckets_s counts the seconds both buckets wanted, 300 to site and 5 to api, the 5 in the slot api takes at 16:03:30, and contested_leads_s the seconds both projects' leads wanted, all api's.
